notes:
- **Stability is a success ratio again, not a latency score.** On a live 2026-11-19 session the screen showed 60-66% while the tunnel answered all 12 probes in its window and carried 20-35 KB/s; the old formula gave latency variation a 40% share, so a perfectly reachable tunnel could never look better than 60%. It also published 100% after a single successful probe. Stability now reads "—" until two checks exist, then reports the share that got through; latency variation is no longer treated as instability.
- **The displayed ping is a real round trip.** It used to be the duration of a full HTTPS probe (DNS + TCP + TLS + 204), which on the same session produced "ping 17000 ms" at the first cycle and 5.7 s medians while the carrier's own RTT was ~370 ms. A TCP handshake through the tunnel now measures the ping; the HTTPS probe's transaction time is kept separately as the guard's slowness evidence. Find Best's latency gate reads the real RTT too, so a 400 ms path is no longer rejected because one request took 5 s.
- **The home list has the sort picker, and the misleading list orders are gone.** The Servers tab's 7d+/30d+ uptime chips are removed, and the app-score chip plus the "App score" and "Long-lived" orders are no longer offered: on this network long uptime predicted the congested public cluster, and a score built mostly from unknown inputs did not predict a usable tunnel. Sorting is available directly on the home list.
- **Settings → Battery** shows whether Android is optimizing this app and opens the system's own exemption dialog. Doze can suspend the packet pump while the screen is off, which looks exactly like the relay dropping the session. The exemption is never granted silently; the user confirms it in Android's dialog.
